text.p: The 2.2 billion marks in risk provisions announced by Bankgesellschaft Berlin are a one-time action to give the bank a secure footing, departing chairman Hubertus Moser said in a television interview.
The provisions "are to give this enterprise a clean slate for the future," Moser told broadcaster N-TV. Allegations the bank lost one billion marks in bad real estate loans are incorrect, he said.

"The risk provisions ... are not only for real estate, they are for the bank's overall portfolio," said Moser, whose resignation was announced late Friday at the same time as the surprisingly large risk provisions.
The reserves were needed due to the continued difficult business situation in Germany, particularly in Berlin and formerly communist east Germany, he said.
The important thing is that the bank is able to solve its problems itself, he said.
Klaus Wowereit, budget spokesman for the Social Democrats in Berlin, said the change in management was overdue at Bankgesellschaft.
"Berliner Bank was involved in almost every company that failed," clearly a sign of management problems, Wowereit said. The state government of Berlin owns more than 50 percent of Bankgesellschaft.
